# HarshaVardhan Aakanti

> Personal site of HarshaVardhan Aakanti (Harsha Aakanti), an Information Security Analyst specialising in AI-driven SOC automation, detection engineering, threat hunting and incident response. The homepage is the blog: practical articles written from day-to-day SOC work. The profile lives on the About page.

All articles are written by HarshaVardhan Aakanti. Case details are anonymised and sanitised. The site is plain HTML with no login and no forms.

## Profile

- [About](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/about/): Background, the SOC alert pipeline, skills, sanitised case files, things he has built, career journey and credentials.
- [Home](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/): Featured and latest articles, topics, search and FAQ.

## Articles

- [How I used AI to build and run my portfolio website](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/how-i-used-ai-to-build-my-portfolio-website/): How I run a plain HTML portfolio with an AI assistant: faster fonts, blog search, AdSense with consent, and the steps that still needed a human. (published 2026-10-24)
- [Cutting L1 triage from 15 minutes to 30 seconds](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/ai-assisted-soc-alert-triage/): How an AI-assisted enrichment pipeline cut first-pass SOC alert triage from 15 minutes to 30 seconds, how it is built, and what it still gets wrong. (published 2026-10-24)
- [Tuning detections to remove 35% of false positives](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/reduce-siem-false-positives-detection-tuning/): A detection tuning playbook: how I cut false positives from custom SIEM rules by about 35% without losing coverage, with before and after examples. (published 2026-10-23)
- [Can LLMs be trusted in the SOC?](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/llm-security-risks-in-the-soc/): The real risks of LLMs in security operations, from prompt injection in alert data to hallucinated IOCs, and the guardrails that make them safe. (published 2026-10-22)
- [A threat hunt walkthrough, from hypothesis to detection](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/threat-hunting-walkthrough-llmjacking-aws/): A step-by-step threat hunt: an LLMjacking hypothesis, CloudTrail queries for AI model enumeration, triage of the results and the detection that followed. (published 2026-10-21)
- [Detection-as-code: treating detection rules like software](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/detection-as-code/): A practical guide to detection as code: SIEM rules in Git, tests against sample logs, peer review in pull requests and deployment through CI. (published 2026-10-20)
- [Incident response lessons from the field](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/incident-response-lessons-learned/): Anonymised incident response lessons from real SOC work: the mistakes that cost time or evidence, and what I would do differently next time. (published 2026-10-19)
- [From offensive security to blue team](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/from-offensive-security-to-blue-team/): What three years of bug bounty hunting taught me about SOC defence: thinking in attack paths, reading alerts like an intruder, and what to unlearn. (published 2026-10-18)
- [A SOC analyst's starter kit](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/soc-analyst-starter-kit/): A starter kit for new SOC analysts: the free tools worth learning, the skills that matter in year one, and the habits that make analysts trustworthy. (published 2026-10-17)
- [MFA is not your last line of defense](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/mfa-is-not-your-last-line-of-defense/): Info-stealers lift session cookies and OAuth tokens, so attackers skip the login and MFA entirely. What SOC teams should detect and change instead. (published 2026-10-16)
- [AI will not replace L1 SOC analysts](https://harshaaakanti.github.io/writing/ai-will-not-replace-l1-soc-analysts/): How enterprise LLMs and the Model Context Protocol cut first-pass SOC triage from 15 minutes to 30 seconds, and why that augments analysts instead of replacing them. (published 2026-10-10)
